rule: Negative subject focus uses the embedded/subjunctive negative aan fused with baa/ayaa rather than ordinary main-clause ma.
source: John I. Saeed, Somali (1999), Simple Sentences focus discussion; Heine & Reh (1984), Grammaticalization and Reanalysis in African Languages; John I. Saeed, The Functions of Focus in Somali
note: Unaccented baan is orthographically ambiguous with baa + 1sg aan in other constructions. The project therefore requires an exact reviewed negative predicate before assigning the negative-subject-focus reading.

rule: When negation co-occurs with focus, Somali uses a reduced subjunctive. In the simple aspect the reduced negative form does not distinguish present from past and does not distinguish person/number.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar (University of Gothenburg, Aug. 2023), p. 94, Reduced subjunctive forms
source_principle: Reduced subjunctive forms are used with negation plus focus; simple heesin serves both past and present and is person/number neutral.
project_execution: Reuse only exact project morphology already reviewed as person-neutral negative simple forms (for example cunin, iman/imanin, aqoon). In negative focus, reinterpret them contextually as reduced_subjunctive_simple with temporal scope present_or_past. No suffix derivation.

rule: When negation co-occurs with focus, progressive reduced subjunctive forms likewise do not distinguish present from past or person/number.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar (University of Gothenburg, Aug. 2023), p. 94, Reduced subjunctive forms
source_principle: Reduced progressive heesayn(in) is listed for both past and present subjunctive under negation plus focus.
project_execution: Reuse only exact project morphology already reviewed as person-neutral negative past-progressive surfaces (for example cunayn/cunaynin and imanayn/imanaynin). In negative focus, reinterpret them contextually as reduced_subjunctive_progressive with temporal scope present_or_past. No unseen form is generated.

rule: A common-noun subject focused by negative baan/ayaan remains in the absolute/non-subject case, as in affirmative baa/ayaa subject focus. The negative reading is assigned only when the predicate independently supplies reviewed negative evidence.
source: Heine & Reh subject-focus case rule plus Saeed negative-focus rule
note: Do not globally reinterpret baan/ayaan as negative because they can overlap subject-clitic spellings in non-subject focus.

rule: The same Gothenburg reduced-subjunctive table also lists habitual heesi jirin and future heesi doonin, but those constructions are deliberately deferred to separate implementation stages.
source: Morgan Nilsson, Beginner's Somali Grammar (University of Gothenburg, Aug. 2023), p. 94
project_execution: Do not infer habitual or future negative focus from the simple/progressive bridge in this stage.
